No network operations, dynamic downloads, or suspicious commands (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`) occur during packaging.

The package replaces and conflicts with `aur-reviewer`, indicating a name change or fork, which is common in AUR. There is no evidence of obfuscated code, unauthorized data exfiltration, or execution of unchecked remote content. The build process is transparent and limited to the declared source. While the actual scripts (`yay-review`, `yay-reviewer-hook`) are not visible here, their installation paths and names align with the package's described purpose. No supply-chain red flags are present.
</details>
